title: Smoke harness for batch/cache config sanity checks
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Build a lightweight, fast-running smoke harness that validates batch/cache configuration recommendations before they are auto-applied. The harness is intended to quickly detect high-severity quality regressions introduced by batching or prefix/KV cache changes using a small, representative set of golden prompts and traffic-shaped synthetic requests. It should execute in under 3 minutes per config candidate and provide deterministic pass/fail signals and detailed diffs to the recommendations engine so we can block unsafe auto-applies and enable fast rollback when necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Smoke harness runs against a config candidate in <= 3 minutes for our baseline /chat and /generate routes
Runs a curated set of 40 golden prompts (mix of short/long, long-context, instruction-style) and computes similarity and task-level metrics

Rejects config candidates when any of: token-level perplexity increases > 10% on golden set, semantic similarity (embedding cosine) drops > 0.08 for >= 3 prompts, or structured output field drops below configured thresholds
Produces machine-readable result artifact (JSON) with per-prompt deltas, threshold triggers, and top-3 counterexample prompts
Can be invoked in shadow mode (no apply) and in pre-apply gate mode integrated with the config applier service
API and CLI available for ad-hoc runs; results pushed to the pull-request and automation dashboard with one-click rollback links
Unit & integration tests for harness logic and threshold evaluation implemented and land in the PR
steps: Design a compact golden prompt corpus (40 prompts) across chat/generation/structured-output -- coordinate with Applied ML and QA to finalize prompts
Implement harness runner that loads candidate config (batch size, KV cache policy, cache TTL, quantization tag) and spins up a short-lived inference sandbox with synthetic traffic shaping
Instrument metrics: token-perplexity, normalized embedding similarity, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and structured-field validation checks
Implement threshold evaluator and mapping from metric deltas to pass/fail reasons (configurable by label)
Wire harness to the config applier: shadow-run on candidate proposals; if fail then block auto-apply and create incident ticket with artifact
Add CLI and REST entrypoints and a lightweight dashboard view showing recent smoke runs and failure patterns
Create a rollout playbook describing when to bypass smoke tests (emergency patches) and who signs off for manual apply/rollback
notes: Goal is fast feedback, not exhaustive regression testing — full regression suite remains the eval-run harness in ENG-99211
We should prioritize short latency for runs; avoid long synthetic traces or expensive eval metrics that slow down gate decisions
Thresholds chosen conservatively to prefer false positives (blocking) over false negatives — safety-first for production requests
Potential trade-off: small golden set may miss low-frequency regressions; mitigated by combining smoke-blocking with canary/gradual rollout policies
We will reuse existing golden embeddings pipeline and the runtime test harness to minimize infra work
Integration with Sandbox infra requires a new ephemeral credentials flow; coordinate with Security for short-lived keys
